## Overview

This vignette demonstrates how to extract an ontology bundle from a SQL DDL
file in a few lines of R code.

## Prerequisites

```{r setup}
library(ontologyDiscoverR)
```

## Choosing a model

ontologyDiscoverR talks to language models through
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org), so it works with any provider ellmer
supports. Nothing is hard-coded: you choose the provider and model, and if you
choose none, discovery stops with an error explaining how to set one.

Pass a Chat object to `discover_session()` (each request gets a fresh clone,
so separate calls never share conversation history):

```{r providers}
# Anthropic (reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
sess <- discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_anthropic())

# OpenAI (reads OPENAI_API_KEY)
sess <- discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1"))

# Google Gemini (reads GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY)
sess <- discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_google_gemini())

# Ollama, running locally: nothing leaves your machine
sess <- discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_ollama(model = "llama3.3"))
```

You can also pass a `"provider/model"` string, which goes to `ellmer::chat()`,
or a function `function(system_prompt)` that returns a Chat:

```{r strings}
sess <- discover_session("demo", llm = "openai/gpt-4.1")
sess <- discover_session("demo", llm = function(sp) {
  ellmer::chat_azure_openai(model = "my-deployment", system_prompt = sp)
})
```

To set a default for every session, use an option or an environment variable
(for example in `.Rprofile` / `.Renviron`):

```{r defaults}
options(ontologyDiscoverR.chat = "anthropic")
Sys.setenv(ONTOLOGYDISCOVERR_CHAT = "ollama/llama3.3")
```

The order is: the `llm` argument, then the option, then the environment
variable. The provider and model used are stored in `sess$llm_info`, and every
candidate records them as `extracted_by` (for example `"openai/gpt-4.1"`), so
runs with different models can be compared.

Extraction uses structured output (`$chat_structured()`) when the provider
supports it. Otherwise the answer is parsed from text, with one retry that
shows the model its parse error.

**Small local models.** Models under roughly 30B parameters extract less
reliably: they miss entities, invent properties and sometimes break the JSON
format. Smaller chunks help, because each request then covers less text:

```{r chunks}
sess <- dis_extract(sess, chunk_tokens = 3000)
# or for every call:
options(ontologyDiscoverR.chunk_tokens = 3000)
```

The default is 8000 tokens per chunk. Values of 2000-4000 suit 7-14B models;
review their candidates with a higher `min_confidence` before building the
bundle.

## Step 1: Create a session and add your schema

```{r session}
sess <- discover_session("hospital-demo", llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1"))
sess <- dis_add_file(sess, "path/to/hospital-schema.sql")
```

You can also point at a live database:

```{r db}
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)

con  <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "hospital.ddb")
sess <- dis_add_db(sess, con, label = "hospital-db")
```

## Step 2: Run extraction

```{r extract}
sess <- dis_extract(sess, verbose = TRUE)
```

This runs three LLM passes per source:
1. **Pass 1**: Extract object types and their properties
2. **Pass 2**: Extract link types (relationships between objects)
3. **Pass 3**: Extract action types and concept hints

After extraction, candidates are deduplicated and merged across sources.

## Step 3: Review (optional)

```{r review, eval=FALSE}
sess <- dis_review(sess)
```

The Shiny review app lets you approve or reject each candidate, edit properties,
and resolve conflicts before building the bundle.

## Step 4: Export to bundle

```{r bundle}
bundle <- dis_to_bundle(
  sess,
  bundle_id   = "hospital-v1",
  bundle_name = "Hospital Management Ontology"
)

# The result is a canonical ontologySpecR bundle, already checked with
# ontologySpecR::validate_bundle(). Write it to JSON:
ontologySpecR::write_bundle(bundle, "hospital-bundle.json")
```

## Quick summary

```{r summary}
dis_summary(sess)
```
